directories.purpose: Project landing page — what it is, its goals, high-level overview.
System design, component relationships, data flow. Explains the current shape; ADRs explain why.
API reference — prefer auto-generated; hand-update only when no generator exists.
Hand-written usage guides — auth flow, patterns, worked examples. No CI safety net.
End-user onboarding, features, FAQ. Omit entirely for projects with no end-user surface.
Every env var and config option — required vs optional, example values.
Architecture Decision Records — why we chose X over Y. Internal only.
Post-hoc bug write-ups — root cause, fix, prevention. Internal only.
Operational procedures written before something breaks. Internal only.

rules.when: Setup steps, commands, or usage instructions changed.
rules.why: README must always reflect current reality and be readable in under a minute.

rules.when: A new feature, integration point, or system boundary was introduced.
rules.why: Architecture docs explain the current shape — how pieces fit together technically.

rules.when: A public function, class, endpoint, or module signature was added or changed.
rules.why: API reference tracks the public surface. Prefer auto-generation; hand-update only when no generator exists.

rules.when: Auth flow, a usage pattern, or a worked example changed in a way a caller would notice.
rules.why: Guides are hand-written with no CI safety net — update in the same change, not later.

rules.when: An env var or config option was added, removed, or renamed.
rules.why: Configuration docs are what people reach for mid-setup-failure. A stale entry is worse than a missing one.

rules.when: A significant architectural decision was made that a new contributor would reasonably make differently without knowing the context.
rules.why: ADRs capture the why behind decisions, not the current shape. Internal only — not synced to the docs site.

rules.when: Something broke and took real diagnosis to fix.
rules.why: Bug write-ups prevent re-diagnosing the same class of problem, including by future agents. Internal only.

rules.when: There is a procedure to follow when a specific operational situation occurs.
rules.why: Runbooks are written before something breaks as a procedure to follow, not after as a record. Internal only.

default.why: If no rule matches but documentation is warranted, update the project landing page.

note: Multiple rules can match. Write or update all matching docs in the same change, not later.
